title: Extract the documentation machinery (docs-doctor, probe executor, jot) from abacus
description: The doc-governance tooling is general-purpose but currently lives in the abacus checkout: tools/docs_doctor.py, tools/probe_executor.py (with run_bounded), tools/test_docs_doctor.py + test_probe_executor.py, and later the jot/jot-review funnel from build step 3. The governing spec (PROPOSAL-funnel-and-docs-doctor.md, operator-approved v20) is likewise general. Cross-repo operation is already demonstrated - this repo's corpus is checked by the abacus copy of docs-doctor today - but two hardcoded abacus-isms make that portability partly illusory and MUST be externalized before or during the move: (1) MODULE_RE at docs_doctor.py:34 hardcodes the abacus module-contract path shape, and (2) BEAD_RE at docs_doctor.py:37 hardcodes the bead:abacus- forward-citation prefix, so a bead:skills- citation in THIS repo is silently unchecked (verified 2026-08-12: zero such citations exist yet, which is why the cross-repo run looked clean). Both belong in the per-repo manifest or the workflow-contract adapter that skills-xg9 already specifies for north-star - one adapter concept serving skills and tools alike. Also externalize the tracker command surface (br --no-db show in the tracker_status probe and the .beads/issues.jsonl reverse-scan input) via the same adapter. SEQUENCING: do not start before abacus-42w closes - the abacus corpus retrofit is the tool's acceptance evidence and extracting mid-build strands it. OPEN SCOPE QUESTION for the operator: this repo is named and chartered for SKILLS; docs-doctor is a CLI tool, not a skill. Whether it lives here (broadening the charter to agent workflow infrastructure) or in a separate tooling repo is exactly the kind of boundary the founding NORTH-STAR.md establish-mode run (skills-xg9 item 5) should settle - run that first, then site this work per the ratified thesis. Acceptance: tools run from their new home against at least two repos with no hardcoded consumer-repo identifiers; abacus consumes them via its own adapter; the abacus copies are retired in the same landing.
design: PIN ANALYSIS - why no lock entry is needed. abacus pins br/bv/herdr because its PRODUCT code wraps their CLI and JSON output with no in-band version negotiation: a silent format change breaks an adapter at runtime. jot is different in kind - it is dev tooling with zero product-runtime coupling, and its wire format carries schema_version in every record with bad_schema_version as a typed refusal, so a version-skewed drain fails closed BY THE FORMAT rather than by a checksum lock. The format is the pin, and it is a better pin: it travels with the data instead of with the consuming repo. RECOMMENDED ADDITION: docs-doctor has no equivalent in-band version - its compatibility surface is docs-corpus.json plus the doc-meta grammar, protected only accidentally by the frozen regex_semantics/glob_semantics literal checks. Add an explicit schema_version to docs-corpus.json during the extraction so the manifest self-declares its contract version the way jot events do; then neither tool needs an external pin. Consumers record at most a minimum-version line in their agent contract, not a lock file.
notes: CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED 2026-08-12. The work moved to the jot repo epic jot-met at ~/dev-environment/jot (remote git@github-personal:DylanDelliColli/jot.git) after the operator ruled the documentation machinery gets its own repo rather than living here. jot-met has eight sequenced children: repo foundation, spec migration with a provenance block, tool migration plus abacus retirement, the class-library/membership manifest split, externalizing abacus-specific identifiers, pinning br, the MVP build of jot and jot-review, and bead/citation migration. Every piece of analysis this bead accumulated - the pin reasoning, the jot portability profile, the build-location fork - was carried into jot-met design and notes fields first. Do not restart this work here. PROVIDER QUIRK observed while closing: br close refused this issue with the message all specified issues were already closed or not found, which was false - it was open. It appears br close skips an issue that still depends on an open blocker (this one depended on skills-xg9). br update --status closed worked. The error message is misleading; do not trust it as evidence that an issue does not exist.

title: council first live acceptance run on a real contested decision
description: The council skill aligned at r5 in abacus with its first live run designated as the acceptance test - it has never run. Execute one full council on a genuinely contested decision (candidates from recent abacus work: the tree-claim TTL amendment shape, the worktree dispatch protocol, or any operator-nominated fork). The run must honor the skill contract in skills/council/SKILL.md: frozen review subject (exact commit or brief-embedded text with hash), herdr version recorded verbatim in the manifest, owner ledger initialized on disk, full reviewer responses captured into the ledger, and the brief passing the reader test (a reader given only brief.md can state the decision under review). Record every deviation the run surfaces as findings on this bead - the run is the test, so gaps are results, not embarrassments. Acceptance: completed run artifacts + a findings list; skill amendments (if any) get their own review round; README.md validation ledger updated in the landing commit.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: Predecessor handoff (w1:p6, retiring) — settled subject choice. Do NOT use the abacus candidates listed in the description (tree-claim TTL amendment, worktree dispatch protocol): re-adjudicating settled abacus work violates the no-re-litigation rule and would waste the acceptance run. USE A LIVE QUESTION IN THIS REPO. Chosen subject: the governance class for skills/*/SKILL.md. Rationale: the skill loader requires clean frontmatter and the closed world requires a doc-meta block - a direct, irreducible conflict with at least three defensible resolutions (sidecar rows, a metadata-exempt class, deliberate exclusion). A decision with an obvious answer would make the acceptance run prove nothing. This also closes an open decision carried on skills-xg9 item 4. OPEN META-QUESTION nobody has raised, decide before the run starts: because this run is itself the skill's acceptance test, the run wants review too - settle up front whether the review lane (w1:p7) reviews the council OUTPUT (manifest, ledger, brief, protocol adherence) or only the DECISION it produced. The skill contract in skills/council/SKILL.md is silent on it. Council has no dependency relationship to north-star. Prior alignment context: git show 9c96d4a:docs/history/SKILL-council-review-r5.md from the abacus checkout (verified resolves 2026-08-12).

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: CORRECTION to the preceding comment: the review lane is w1J:p2, not w1:p7 (w1:p7 is being retired per operator ruling 2026-08-12). The open meta-question is unchanged in substance and still must be settled before the run starts - decide whether w1J:p2 reviews the council RUN OUTPUT (manifest, owner ledger, brief, protocol adherence) or only the DECISION the run produced. Because w1J:p2 is a fresh pane with no doctrine in context, the question gets sharper: reviewing the run output requires the reviewer to hold the skill contract in skills/council/SKILL.md and the r5 round, so if that is the choice, prime it with both before dispatch.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: OPERATOR RULING 2026-08-12, settling the review-scope meta-question raised in the earlier comments. The review lane reviews ONLY THE FINAL DECISION, not the run output. Rationale, operator: the council exists to perform the intermediate review, so a separate reviewer re-examining the run would duplicate the skill's whole purpose, and re-examining the decision's substance would violate the no-re-litigation rule besides. REFINEMENT accepted in the same exchange, to close the one gap that ruling leaves. This run produces two artifacts: a decision about skill-definition governance, and acceptance evidence that the council skill works at all. The council reviews the subject; nothing inside the run checks whether the run's own machinery held (frozen review subject, herdr version recorded verbatim in the manifest, owner ledger initialized on disk, full reviewer responses captured, brief passing the reader test). Because the same agent runs the council and would otherwise certify it, that is self-grading, which is the exact failure the sibling north-star skill forbids when it requires a missing judge capability to fail closed without self-grading. RESOLUTION, no extra ceremony and no second round: dispatch the lane to judge the decision only, and instruct it that if the brief, ledger, and manifest do not let it judge that decision, the gap IS a reportable finding. Protocol adherence is then observed as a byproduct of the decision review rather than as a separate audit. Do not commission a review of the run output as its own round.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: DEFERRED by operator ruling 2026-08-12: lowest-value work available right now, paused in favor of finishing north-star (fixture, then user-global install). Nothing is lost by pausing - the subject choice (skill-definition governance) and the review-scope ruling (the lane reviews the final decision only, with artifact-insufficiency counting as a reportable finding) are recorded in the comments above and remain valid whenever council resumes. ONE COUPLING TO WATCH: skill-definition governance was routed here for adjudication rather than decided on the extraction bead. That decision is now unanswered for as long as council stays deferred, so if the extraction bead reaches the point of needing it, decide it directly with the operator instead of waiting for a council run. title: north-star skill: Test values interview module in establish and revise modes
description:
Operator direction 2026-08-15 (decided in the abacus session, edits placed where most logical): the north-star skill's establish and revise modes gain a Test values interview module, so every repository that runs /north-star gets a repo-level declaration of which test classes are high-value.

What it produces: a required "Test values" section in the repository's NORTH-STAR.md — a short ranked table of test classes with, per class: value rank, the reason it earns that rank in THIS repo, and its runtime cost class (effectively-free vs expensive). Values and ranks only — binding numeric caps for expensive classes deliberately do NOT live in the north star (its own contract sends binding numbers to ADRs; the consuming repo's planning ADR carries caps and cites the ranking). Revise mode can amend the section like any other; establish mode asks for it.

MVP-first (binding ruling, this repo): the simplest interview that works — a handful of questions surfacing the repo's test classes, their relative value, and which are expensive. No machinery, no validation tooling, no cross-repo enforcement; the consuming planning flow (abacus-plan, in the abacus repo) is responsible for reading and enforcing.

Evidence case: the abacus suite doubled (45 → 89 tests) in one execution loop on 2026-08-15; runtime concentrates ~entirely in one class (real-process integration), and the planning flow had no repo-level statement of test-class value to price against. Full reviewed proposal (bloat + spec validated, both fresh Codex contexts) archived in the abacus session of that date.

Process per this repo's contract: cross-lineage review before landing (the established Codex review pane, primed with the MVP-first ruling and the scale-not-shape scope guard; recompute the pane occupant before dispatch — recovery pointers on skills-xg9). The dogfood acceptance is running the revised establish/revise mode against a real repo (abacus's revise session for its Test values section is the natural first run).

File footprint

skills/north-star/SKILL.md

Acceptance Criteria

- Establish mode's interview includes the Test values questions and writes the section; revise mode can amend it under the existing amendment-log conventions.
- The section's format matches what the consuming planning flow reads: class, rank, why, cost class — no numeric caps.
- Cross-lineage review completed per repo contract before landing.
- [no-test] in the code sense — skill prose; the acceptance test is the first live interview run with the operator.

title: north-star check-mode fixture (mode is UNTRUSTED until this lands)
description: The north-star skill aligned at r4 in abacus with check mode explicitly untrusted until a fixture exists. Build a hermetic fixture suite for check mode per the acceptance list in skills/north-star/SKILL.md (~line 170-180): the two-observation gate, verdict fold, check-record write shape (north-star-checks/<ULID>.md, never edited after creation), addenda as distinct event-ULID paths with no merge conflict, and record replay. Reuse the proven harness patterns from abacus tools/test_docs_doctor.py: temp git repos, baseline-must-be-clean design, expect_findings-style result-bound assertions, stub providers on PATH, and tools/probe_executor.py (import from the abacus checkout until the executor is extracted). Acceptance: fixture green from this repo root; the UNTRUSTED marker comes off README.md in the same commit.
notes: SCOPE GUARD added 2026-08-12 under the MVP-first ruling now in AGENTS.md. This bead tells you to reuse the harness patterns from the docs-doctor fixture. Reuse the SHAPE - temp git repos, a baseline that must run clean, result-bound assertions, stub providers on PATH - and explicitly NOT the scale. That suite is 176 cases for a 1400-line linter that gates every documentation change in a repository. Check mode is an operator-in-the-loop interview procedure whose failures are visible to a human in real time; it needs enough cases to make the verdict fold and the record-write trustworthy, and no more. If the fixture starts growing past the point where each new case is defending an observed failure rather than an imagined one, stop and ship it. The UNTRUSTED marker comes off README.md when the mode is trustworthy, not when the suite is exhaustive.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: Predecessor handoff (w1:p6, retiring) — settled answers. SEQUENCING: xg9 item 5 (establish run) does NOT gate this bead. A fixture must supply a synthetic NORTH-STAR.md anyway; coupling the suite to the real thesis would bind it to a changing document. Establish is schedule-blocked (operator-interactive), not dependency-blocked, so it must not gate agent-schedulable work. Build h1u now. SCOPE DISTINCTION the bead text does not draw: the fixture proves the MECHANISM (verdict fold, check-record write shape, addenda as distinct event-ULID paths, replay). It does not prove the mode yields a verdict worth having. Read the UNTRUSTED marker as mechanism-trustworthy. A first real check against the founded thesis is a separate cheap validation to run after establish - note it here, do not expand this bead's scope to cover it. PROBE_EXECUTOR: the import instruction in the description was pattern-matching from the docs-doctor fixture, not analysis. First prove you need bounded subprocess execution at all; run_bounded is ~40 lines and inlinable. If genuinely needed, build against the abacus checkout and re-point later - jot-met.3 is gated on an unscheduled worker landing plus operator clearance (indefinite), and re-pointing is one line. THE ACTUAL SPEC FOR THIS FIXTURE is the r4 review round, where check mode was judged untrusted - it records what the reviewer thought was unproven. Recover from the abacus checkout: git show 9c96d4a:docs/history/SKILL-north-star-review-r4.md (verified resolves 2026-08-12). Read it before drafting.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: SPEC LOCATED - the fixture is bounded by the skill text itself, not by judgment. skills/north-star/SKILL.md, section 'Before relying on check mode - falsification fixture', enumerates exactly SEVEN cases, and r4 confirms they are the consequential branches: (1) missing judge capability fails closed without self-grading; (2) judge receives no parent turns and its payload-only instruction is present; (3) seeded cases hit all four verdicts including an overlap resolved by decision order; (4) malformed judge output causes no action; (5) a material trim reaches the operator before mutation; (6) two concurrent worktrees produce distinct check records with no merge conflict; (7) a stored record replays thesis snapshot, case, result, rationale, dispute, and disposition under the initial-record-then-addenda-in-ULID-order rule. This settles the MVP scope guard quantitatively: seven cases is the target, and a case that is not defending one of these seven branches is scope creep. Compare 176 for docs-doctor. PASS-RECORD SHAPE is also specified and is easy to get wrong: passage is recorded bound to the skill blob hash AND the exact adapter/model/tool-policy combination, as immutable files under north-star-checks/fixture/ keyed by that combination. A changed skill blob, adapter, model, or tool policy MUST produce a lookup miss, never a stale pass. Untested combination equals untrusted is the default state, not an error - so the fixture has to prove the miss, not just the hit. PROBE_EXECUTOR determination, resolving the predecessor's open question from the spec rather than from pattern-matching: cases 1, 2, and 4 require a judge-provider seam that can be made absent, inspected for prompt isolation, and made to emit malformed output, so stub providers on PATH are genuinely required. Bounded subprocess execution is NOT thereby required - a plain subprocess call with a timeout covers it. Do not import tools/probe_executor.py from the abacus checkout unless a case is written that actually needs run_bounded semantics. NOTE for skills-xg9 item 1: the Boundaries section of this SKILL.md hardcodes two more abacus bindings the adapter must absorb - the br comments add append-safe operation with its warning that br update --notes replaces the field, and stock br create being unable to set acceptance atomically.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: PARKED by operator ruling 2026-08-12. Do not execute this bead as written. Reasoning, recorded so a future agent does not simply restart it: this bead orders a seven-case falsification fixture for check mode, but check mode has never been invoked once, and neither has establish mode. The skill directory contains exactly one file, SKILL.md, with no implementation anywhere in the workspace, so the fixture has nothing to execute - the instruction to reuse the docs-doctor test harness presumes a program analogous to that linter, and none exists here. Building it would mean first writing a runner in order to have something to test, which is machinery invented to satisfy a test rather than to serve a user. That is precisely the pattern the MVP-first ruling in AGENTS.md was written to stop, and this bead is its clearest instance: an approved design document is never a build order. Note the review-round subtlety: round four ACCEPTED this design and judged it internally consistent, but it assessed the artifact within its chosen scope, which is exactly the blindness the ruling names as mechanism (a). Round four also explicitly considered and rejected the cheaper alternative, recording that direct operator adjudication is cheaper but loses the bounded independent challenge - a rejection that only looks correct from inside the chosen scope. WHAT REPLACES THIS WORK: nothing, for now. Check mode stays exactly as written and honestly marked untrusted, which the skill text itself calls the default state and not an error. Establish and revise modes are unaffected and usable today. REOPEN THIS ONLY on observed evidence: after establish mode has actually been used and someone has wanted a check badly enough to run one, the real failures of that run become the case list. Build against those, not against the seven imagined branches.

title: Reverse-citation defect reintroduced in bead comments (3 foreign-repo paths, unfixable in place)
description: Docs-doctor on this repo went from the predecessor baseline of 4 reverse-citation findings to 8. Four were new, authored by w1J:p1 on 2026-08-12 while recording the skill-dev handoff. One is the acceptable planned-output kind matching the existing baseline. The other three are the reverse-citation hygiene defect this repo already ruled on at commit caa709d: bare relative paths naming the archived north-star round-four review and the archived council round-five review, written into comments on the north-star fixture bead, the council acceptance bead, and the extraction bead. Those two files exist only in the abacus checkout, so docs-doctor resolves the paths against this repo and reports unresolved_reference. They are rot-shaped rather than planned-output-shaped, which is exactly the distinction the hygiene rule protects. NOT FIXABLE IN PLACE: br comments supports only add and list, with no edit or delete, so those tokens cannot be reworded. The predecessor could repair their equivalent slip because it lived in a description, which br update --description can rewrite. TWO METHODOLOGY FINDINGS worth carrying to the workflow-contract adapter on the extraction bead, item 1. First, the append-safe record operation that the north-star skill mandates for durability is the same operation that makes a citation-hygiene mistake permanent, so the adapter must require foreign-repo references to be written non-path-like at capture time - name the repo and the object in prose, or cite the commit hash alone - because no later correction path exists. Second, discovered while filing this very issue: the first version of this description quoted the offending paths verbatim in order to describe them, which reintroduced all three tokens and pushed the count from 8 to 11. A defect report about citation hygiene cannot quote the citation it is reporting. The prose-reference technique was then confirmed to work: a comment added to the council bead in the same session using prose references produced zero new findings. REMEDIATION for the three unfixable comment tokens, operator to choose: accept as a declared known-degradation with a recorded reason, add a docs-doctor allowance for tracker comments citing foreign repositories, or rebuild the affected comments if br ever gains an edit path. Verify with the docs-doctor invocation given in AGENTS.md, run from this repo root.

title: Choose which docs-doctor copy this repo invokes once jot's port lands
description: Decision, not a code change. Today AGENTS.md invokes python3 ~/dev-environment/abacus-v1/tools/docs_doctor.py --repo . - the eleven-check copy. That path is stable: abacus-v1 is a frozen parts bin and jot-met.3 no longer deletes its tools directory, so nothing forces a move. THE CHOICE: jot is receiving only the four structural checks (check_metadata, check_corpus_index, check_corpus_index_agreement, plus classification and path confinement). Seven are deferred there - check_supersession, check_probes, check_bead_citations, check_historical_bytes, check_archive_index, check_reverse_citations, check_evidence_index - deferred by operator ruling as valuable but not MVP, not rejected. WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: this repo's only live docs-doctor findings come from reverse-citations, which is in the deferred seven. Verified 2026-08-13 - two unresolved_reference rows against skills-xg9 (one on its description, one on a comment), aggregate degraded, zero execution errors. Moving to jot's copy makes this repo report clean by removing the check that finds anything, which is the worst reason to look green. OPTIONS: (a) keep invoking the archive copy indefinitely - it is frozen so it cannot drift, and this repo keeps the signal; (b) move to jot's copy and accept that reverse-citations stops running here; (c) move, and separately ask jot to promote reverse-citations out of deferral against this observed need, which is exactly the evidence its deferral was waiting for. ACCEPTANCE: AGENTS.md names one copy and the choice is recorded on this bead. Do not put the reasoning back into AGENTS.md - that file is a behavioral contract and in-flight decisions belong here.
close_reason: Decided by the operator 2026-08-13: this repo moves to jot's four-check copy. Migrated in the same act, because jot's tool requires a conforms_to membership file that the eleven-check archive copy cannot read - the two are no longer interchangeable, so choosing the manifest format IS choosing the copy. docs-corpus.json is now membership at conforms_to 4; the three index files renamed to INDEX.md; index rows reduced to path and claim. The lane's uncommitted addition of SKILL-REVIEW-*.md to inflight_globs was preserved through the rewrite. Aggregate is clean. THE COST IS REAL AND IS RECORDED IN AGENTS.md RATHER THAN LEFT IMPLICIT: this repo reports clean because reverse-citations no longer runs, not because its eight findings against skills-xg9 were fixed. They are still in the tracker. The eleven-check copy remains in the frozen abacus-v1 tree if that signal is wanted back. Option (c) from this bead - asking jot to promote reverse-citations out of deferral - is untaken and remains available; jot has the evidence on its own tracker that the check shapes what gets written in a tracker, which is the argument against promotion that would need answering.

comments.author: w1H-jot-build
comments.text: EVIDENCE UPDATE from the jot build lane, 2026-08-13. jot-met.3 has landed: jot tools now carry the four structural checks with a matching fixture suite. Three corrections to the numbers on this bead. (1) This repo's live finding count is EIGHT, not two - the two unresolved_reference rows against skills-xg9 recorded here were counted before later work added more. Re-verified today against the eleven-check archive copy: aggregate degraded, eight reverse-citations findings, zero execution errors. (2) Running jot's four-check copy against this repo reports aggregate clean with zero findings. So option (b) is not a partial loss of signal, it is a total one: every finding this repo produces today comes from the one check jot did not receive. (3) AGENTS.md now names the archive copy as the eleven-check copy and points here for the choice, per this bead's instruction to keep the reasoning off the contract. The choice itself is untouched and remains this lane's. One note toward option (c): jot deferred reverse-citations partly on evidence that it shapes what gets written in the tracker - twice in jot a bead record was reworded so the check would stop counting. If this repo argues for promotion, that cost is the thing to argue against, and a way to cite a filename without triggering a finding is probably the precondition.

comments.author: ddc
comments.text: Predecessor handoff (w1:p6, retiring) — leanings on the two open decisions. ITEM 4 (governance class for skill definition files): routed to skills-bny as the council acceptance-run subject rather than decided here. Do not settle it unilaterally on this bead. NORTH-STAR-CHECKS RESIDENCY (the skills-repo twin of abacus-uzu): predecessor leaning, held back only to avoid a unilateral record - these records should be EXPLICITLY UNGOVERNED. They are append-only, one per check, unbounded; admitting them to the corpus makes the index grow without bound and forces an index edit on every check run, which is precisely the manually-curated-list failure the taxonomy advisory warned against. They are closest to evidence in kind, but the evidence class assumes a coherent-bundle boundary and a symmetry-checked index built for a handful of authored records, not per-run machine output. Honest classification: generated run output, like ab-results/ in the knowledge fixture, which correctly lives outside the corpus. IMPORTANT NUANCE: the current passing state is accidental, not designed - docs-doctor root discovery only examines root-level .md and docs/**, so north-star-checks/*.md is invisible to it. Make the exclusion explicit as a declared known-non-corpus path, or a future discovery change closes the gap by surprise. REVIEW LANE (AGENTS.md records the requirement but names no pane): predecessor designates w1:p7, the Codex pane that ran all twenty adversarial rounds on the funnel and docs-doctor - it holds the doctrine and ceremony budget in context, returned NOT ALIGNED nine consecutive times rather than rubber-stamping, and recommended freezing when asked for a convergence judgment. Its cwd being abacus is irrelevant; give absolute paths. w1H:p1 is DISQUALIFIED - it is Codex but now the jot build lane, and pairing a builder as reviewer defeats the purpose. If a future session here is Codex rather than Claude, w1H:p2 is jot's designated reviewer - ask the operator for a new pane rather than double-booking it.

comments.author: ddc

The review lane for this repo is w1J:p2, a Codex pane in this session's own workspace with cwd already set to /home/ddc/dev-environment/skills. It supersedes w1:p7 entirely.
